subject: ggvis used in a shiny app: tooltip ability lost after changes of the size of point size

messages.author: 185b691c84b200d6
messages.subject: ggvis used in a shiny app: tooltip ability lost after changes of the size of point size
parts:
Dear all,

the tooltip ability of ggvis in a shiny app is lost after updating the graph with another point size through the sliderInput.
The code delivers the plot in the web browser (Firefox 27.0.1) w/o problems.

Best regards,
Jürgen

The code:

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
all_values <- function(x) {
    if(is.null(x)) return(NULL)
    paste0(names(x), ": ", format(x), collapse = "<br />")
  }

  gv <- reactive({
    ggvis(mtcars, props(x = ~disp, y = ~mpg, size := input$size)) +tooltip(all_values) +
      layer_point()
  })
  observe_ggvis(gv, "my_plot", session)
})

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel(""),
  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput("size", "Area", 10, 1000,20)
  ),
  mainPanel(
    ggvis_output("my_plot")
  )
))

messages.subject: Re: ggvis used in a shiny app: tooltip ability lost after changes of the size of point size
parts:
Jürgen, I think this is likely a bug in ggvis. I believe that the hovering event handlers aren't being set up properly when a new plot spec is sent to the client.

In any case, there's also a subtle but important difference between this app and ones that are auto-generated by ggvis. First, a little background. In Vega (the rendering engine) and ggvis, there are two separate pieces: the spec, which is a declarative grammar-of-graphics description of the plot, and the data. You can change the data without forcing a complete recomputation and redraw of the plot; however, if you change the spec, the plot must be completely redrawn.

In this app you're using shiny::sliderInput, and reading the value in a reactive expression with input$size. Whenever that value changes, the reactive expression is invalidated, and is run again. This runs the ggvis() function call again, and the result is that a new spec and data is sent to the client. When you change the slider, you'll see the whole plot blink, which indicates that a new spec is being used.

Below I've included a modified version of your app. Instead of using shiny::sliderInput, it uses ggvis::input_slider, which is wrapper around sliderInput that returns a _delayed_ reactive object. Notice that this version of the app doesn't refer to input$size or anything like that. Because of this, the reactive expression isn't invalidated when the slider value changes, and it doesn't get re-executed, and a new spec is not sent to the client - only new data. You won't see the blink when you change the slider values with this app. Also, the tooltips will keep working.

(Sorry if this sounds a little opaque -- I'd have to revisit that code in order to give a good description of how delayed reactives are handled behind the scenes.)


A slightly tweaked version of your original app:
========================================
library(shiny)
library(ggvis)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

all_values <- function(x) {
    if(is.null(x)) return(NULL)
    paste0(names(x), ": ", format(x), collapse = "<br />")
  }

  gv <- reactive({
    ggvis(mtcars, props(x = ~disp, y = ~mpg, size := input$size)) +
      tooltip(all_values) +
      layer_point()
  })
  observe_ggvis(gv, "my_plot", session)
}
ui <- pageWithSidebar(

headerPanel(""),
  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput("size", "Area", 10, 1000,20)
  ),
  mainPanel(
    ggvis_output("my_plot")
  )
)

runApp(list(server=server, ui=ui))
========================================


And here's my version of it using ggvis::input_slider:
========================================
library(shiny)
library(ggvis)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

all_values <- function(x) {
    if(is.null(x)) return(NULL)
    paste0(names(x), ": ", format(x), collapse = "<br />")
  }

  gv <- reactive({

size_slider <- input_slider(label = "Area", 10, 1000, 20)
    ggvis(mtcars, props(x = ~disp, y = ~mpg, size := size_slider)) +

tooltip(all_values) +
      layer_point()
  })
  observe_ggvis(gv, "my_plot", session)

output$ggvis_controls <- renderControls(gv, session)
}

ui <- pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel(""),
  sidebarPanel(
    ggvisControlOutput("ggvis_controls", "my_plot")

),
  mainPanel(
    ggvis_output("my_plot")
  )
)

runApp(list(server=server, ui=ui))
========================================


Hope this helps!
-Winston

Am Montag, 3. März 2014 19:29:02 UTC+1 schrieb Winston:
Jürgen, I think this is likely a bug in ggvis. I believe that the hovering event handlers aren't being set up properly when a new plot spec is sent to the client.

In any case, there's also a subtle but important difference between this app and ones that are auto-generated by ggvis. First, a little background. In Vega (the rendering engine) and ggvis, there are two separate pieces: the spec, which is a declarative grammar-of-graphics description of the plot, and the data. You can change the data without forcing a complete recomputation and redraw of the plot; however, if you change the spec, the plot must be completely redrawn.

In this app you're using shiny::sliderInput, and reading the value in a reactive expression with input$size. Whenever that value changes, the reactive expression is invalidated, and is run again. This runs the ggvis() function call again, and the result is that a new spec and data is sent to the client. When you change the slider, you'll see the whole plot blink, which indicates that a new spec is being used.

Below I've included a modified version of your app. Instead of using shiny::sliderInput, it uses ggvis::input_slider, which is wrapper around sliderInput that returns a _delayed_ reactive object. Notice that this version of the app doesn't refer to input$size or anything like that. Because of this, the reactive expression isn't invalidated when the slider value changes, and it doesn't get re-executed, and a new spec is not sent to the client - only new data. You won't see the blink when you change the slider values with this app. Also, the tooltips will keep working.

(Sorry if this sounds a little opaque -- I'd have to revisit that code in order to give a good description of how delayed reactives are handled behind the scenes.)


A slightly tweaked version of your original app:
========================================
library(shiny)
library(ggvis)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  all_values <- function(x) {
    if(is.null(x)) return(NULL)
    paste0(names(x), ": ", format(x), collapse = "<br />")
  }

  gv <- reactive({
    ggvis(mtcars, props(x = ~disp, y = ~mpg, size := input$size)) +
      tooltip(all_values) +
      layer_point()
  })
  observe_ggvis(gv, "my_plot", session)
}

ui <- pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel(""),
  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput("size", "Area", 10, 1000,20)
  ),
  mainPanel(
    ggvis_output("my_plot")
  )
)

runApp(list(server=server, ui=ui))
========================================


And here's my version of it using ggvis::input_slider:
========================================
library(shiny)
library(ggvis)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  all_values <- function(x) {
    if(is.null(x)) return(NULL)
    paste0(names(x), ": ", format(x), collapse = "<br />")
  }

  gv <- reactive({
    size_slider <- input_slider(label = "Area", 10, 1000, 20)
    ggvis(mtcars, props(x = ~disp, y = ~mpg, size := size_slider)) +
      tooltip(all_values) +
      layer_point()
  })
  observe_ggvis(gv, "my_plot", session)

  output$ggvis_controls <- renderControls(gv, session)
}

ui <- pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel(""),
  sidebarPanel(
    ggvisControlOutput("ggvis_controls", "my_plot")
  ),
  mainPanel(
    ggvis_output("my_plot")
  )
)

runApp(list(server=server, ui=ui))
========================================


Hope this helps!
-Winston
